thesis: IPAR is a stretched, richly valued, flat-growth name that Goldman just downgraded on valuation, and it trades above the mean analyst target. RSI is 73.5, price is 8.8% above SMA20 after a 5-day +6.7% run, and the technical card itself says chasing the last close is poor. The tape is a half-day session with thin liquidity inside a high-confidence risk-off regime (QQQ below the 50- and 200-day averages, VIX at the 0.90 percentile), where a high-multiple stock can be sold even though it is defensive. Earnings are not expected to grow into the multiple (forward P/E above trailing), so the upside rests on sentiment alone. The pullback entry needs a dip that may not come, and if it does, the reward/risk is only 1.8 with a stop about 2.4 ATR away.
